summary: Yes: TTLCache.get returns the value at exactly ttl seconds. Decided by 'self.clock() - stored > self.ttl' at cache.py:20 (strict >). Changed from '>=' in e6ed919 (Ana, #12): 'On coarse clocks (time.monotonic ticks in 15 ms steps) entries stored with ttl=1 expired on the first read after a one-tick advance. Serve an entry until it is strictly older than ttl, so ttl is the minimum lifetime.' Observed with a fake clock, ttl=10: age 10 -> v, age 10.001 -> MISS.
